To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the intermittency analysis of multiparticle production data, based on the study of single event data, is improved, taking account of corrections due to the particle momentum reconstruction.

(i) the intermittency analysis of individual events (particle moments) can be improved taking into account corrections for the reconstruction of the particle history in the detector, (ii) these corrections are important for a reliable determination of the intermittency exponent, (iii) the intermittency exponents are found to be in a good agreement with the theoretical prediction of the $\alpha-$model for the case of the $e^+e^-$ annihilation data

the intermittency analysis of individual events is improved by taking into account corrections that arise from reconstruction of the history of a particle shower, that the intermittency of individual events is a sensitive probe of multiplicity fluctuations, and that the intermittency exponent $\tau$ is not a universal parameter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the multiparticle production process in terms of intermittency.
the study of the structure of hadronic events in the high energy limit.
the analysis of the multiplicity fluctuations in high energy hadron collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intermittency is not a phenomenon of multiparticle production, but is a result of the reconstruction of the history of a particle cascades.

intermittency in multiparticle production, as measured by the moments of the multiplicity distributions, is not a property of the underlying cascade process, but rather a consequence of the way the data are analyzed and presented, and of the finite statistics of the data.
the $\alpha$ -model, in spite of its simplicity, is a very good tool to understand and describe intermittency.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can now analyze single event data, and that we have a better understanding of the limitations of the intermittency analysis.}
intermittency analysis of particle multiplicity moments is not a good method for the study of multiparticle production processes.
the intermittency analysis of the multiplicity data is a powerful tool to study multiparticle dynamics in high energy collisions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intermittency analysis of individual event data can be performed with a good precision and the results obtained are consistent with the ones obtained by the standard method.

the intermittency exponent is a quantity which is very sensitive to the underlying physics of particle production and it can serve as a useful tool for the investigation of particle production mechanisms.
the intermittency exponent $\tau$ is not a good measure for the intermittency.
